note: Seeded by the lead from verified loop evidence (ModernizationLoops.md loops 1-5). COBOL-side facts only; no original-Java identifiers.

entries.text: A called program that dispatches on a function or operation code in its linkage area and does arithmetic on caller-supplied operands is a library (kernel), not business logic. Name it after the capability (DecimalKernel, RoundingKernel, DateKernel); its op codes become methods named after the operation the paragraph performs.

evidence.summary: decimal library called with an operation code (loop 5)

entries.text: A paragraph that sets a return or abend code and CALLs CEE3ABD (or ends the run with a non-zero RETURN-CODE) is the abend path; in Java it is an exception type plus a single throw site, named for the failure (e.g. CapacityExceeded), not for the paragraph number.

An FD or I/O record layout is a boundary type (name it ...Record or ...Line after the file's business content). A WORKING-STORAGE group that several paragraphs read and write together as one business value is the domain entity candidate (no Record suffix).

evidence.summary: value groups read and written together by the posting paragraphs

entries.text: A field whose values are all named by 88-levels is an enum; name the enum after what the field classifies (the 88-level names are the constants, expanded from their abbreviations), not after the field's prefix.

evidence.summary: 88-level condition names on status and type codes

entries.text: Counters and accumulators incremented per record and printed at end of job are run statistics: one value type (RunTotals) with named components, not separate fields on the job class.

evidence.summary: end-of-job counts written to the report

entries.text: Shop prefixes (WS-, LK-, a 2-4 letter program or system prefix such as KZ or FS) carry ownership, not meaning. Drop them from Java names; record them in the ledger's legacy id.

evidence.summary: WS- and program-prefixed data names throughout
